# Fall River/New Bedford Line

The term Fall River/New Bedford Line refers to the railroad corridor serving the South Coast cities of Fall River and New Bedford, Massachusetts, both historically and in contemporary usage. Historically, it denotes the New Bedford and Fall River branches of the Old Colony Railroad (later the New York, New Haven and Hartford Railroad) linking those ports to Taunton and the Boston area. In current practice, Massachusetts agencies primarily refer to the corridor and the MBTA’s commuter rail restoration as South Coast Rail, which launched revenue service to Fall River and New Bedford in 2024 via a Middleborough routing (Phase 1), with a longer-term plan to complete a Stoughton routing (Phase 2) that was the subject of the earlier environmental review and federal Record of Decision. This article treats “Fall River/New Bedford Line” as the paired branches to Fall River and New Bedford and summarizes their development from the 19th century to the present MBTA South Coast Rail service, including planning, infrastructure, operations, governance, environmental review, and future plans .

## Naming and scope

- Agencies and project materials primarily use South Coast Rail to describe the MBTA commuter rail restoration to Fall River and New Bedford and the overall program including both Phase 1 (via Middleborough) and Phase 2 (via Stoughton) . 
- The physical rail corridors are typically called by their freight subdivision names: the Fall River Secondary and New Bedford Secondary, owned by the Commonwealth and used by both passenger and freight services . 
- In public-facing MBTA materials after the start of service, timetables and station pages refer to New Bedford Line and Fall River Line branches under the South Coast Rail umbrella . 
- Historically, the branches were components of the Old Colony system and, after 1893, the New York, New Haven and Hartford Railroad; in this context, “Fall River line” can also appear in historical sources, but that phrase historically also referred to combined rail–steamship services to New York and should be distinguished by context .

## History

### 19th and early 20th centuries

- The New Bedford and Taunton Railroad opened in 1840, creating a rail link from New Bedford to Taunton and, via connections, to Boston; the Fall River Branch Railroad opened in the 1840s linking Fall River to the Old Colony network. These and related lines were consolidated into the Old Colony Railroad by the 1870s and leased to the New York, New Haven and Hartford Railroad in 1893, placing both branches in the New Haven system . 
- Through the mid-20th century, frequent passenger service operated between Boston and South Coast communities via the Old Colony network .

### Cessation of prior passenger service and Old Colony revival

- Passenger service on the Old Colony network ended in the 1950s, with the last Old Colony passenger trains discontinued in 1959 amid declining ridership and infrastructure disinvestment, leaving Fall River and New Bedford without direct passenger rail to Boston for decades . 
- MBTA restored commuter rail on portions of the Old Colony system in 1997 (e.g., to Middleborough/Lakeville) but not to the South Coast branches .

### South Coast Rail project development

- Massachusetts initiated the South Coast Rail (SCR) planning process in the 1990s, with extensive state and federal environmental review in the 2000s–2010s. The combined state Final Environmental Impact Report and federal Final Environmental Impact Statement (FEIR/FEIS) was published in 2013, identifying the Stoughton alignment as the preferred alternative for full Boston–Taunton–Fall River/New Bedford service and documenting substantial environmental mitigation requirements, particularly in and near the Hockomock Swamp Area of Critical Environmental Concern in Easton and Raynham . 
- The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers issued a federal Record of Decision (ROD) for the Stoughton alignment in 2017, concluding the federal NEPA process for that route . 
- To deliver service sooner while funding and permitting for the Stoughton route advanced, MassDOT and the MBTA adopted a phased approach in 2018: Phase 1 via Middleborough to initiate service using existing rights-of-way upgraded for passenger speeds and new stations, and Phase 2 to complete the Stoughton alignment later. The Phase 1 Middleborough approach underwent a separate Environmental Assessment under NEPA, culminating in a federal Finding of No Significant Impact in 2020 . 
- Early works and main construction for Phase 1 proceeded during 2019–2024, including track, signals, grade crossing upgrades, bridges, layover facilities, and new stations on the Fall River and New Bedford branches .

### Launch of MBTA service

- The MBTA announced the start of South Coast Rail service effective July 1, 2024, with scheduled commuter rail service from Boston South Station to both Fall River and New Bedford via the existing Old Colony route to Middleborough and the newly upgraded Middleborough Secondary, Fall River Secondary, and New Bedford Secondary . 

## Route and infrastructure

### Ownership and route segments

- The Commonwealth of Massachusetts (MassDOT) owns the Fall River Secondary and New Bedford Secondary, acquired as part of broader rail asset agreements with CSX, and grants freight operating rights on those lines while coordinating passenger improvements with the MBTA . 
- Passenger trains operate from Boston South Station over the MBTA Old Colony mainline to Braintree and the Middleborough/Lakeville Line to a new Middleborough station; from there, the route uses the Middleborough Secondary to Cotley (Taunton) and then diverges southwesterly on the Fall River Secondary to Fall River and southerly on the New Bedford Secondary to New Bedford . 
- The Phase 1 program included track upgrades to passenger standards, new and rehabilitated bridges, new signal systems, Positive Train Control (PTC), passing sidings, and numerous grade crossing safety enhancements across both branches .

### Stations and facilities

All stations opened with the launch of revenue service on July 1, 2024 :

- Middleborough (new station on the Middleborough Secondary) . 
- East Taunton (serving Taunton and the Myles Standish Industrial Park) . 
- Freetown (Assonet/Freetown) . 
- Fall River (downtown Fall River) . 
- Church Street (north New Bedford) . 
- New Bedford (downtown New Bedford) .

Additional facilities:

- Layover yards were constructed to support operations: New Bedford Layover (near the Wamsutta area north of downtown) and Fall River Layover (Weaver’s Cove area), designed to store and service trainsets between trips . 
- All new stations were designed to be fully accessible, with high-level platforms and ADA-compliant features consistent with MBTA standards .

### Signals and train control

- The project installed new signal systems and extended Positive Train Control across the corridor. MBTA commuter rail uses ACSES II PTC on its territory, including the Old Colony and newly equipped South Coast Rail segments for interoperability and safety compliance .

## Operations and service

- Launch date: Revenue service began July 1, 2024 . 
- Service pattern: MBTA schedules provide separate timetables for the New Bedford Line and Fall River Line branches under South Coast Rail. Weekday service includes peak-period inbound and outbound trips and off-peak service; weekend service operates at reduced frequency relative to weekdays . 
- Travel times: Published MBTA timetables show end-to-end scheduled travel times between Boston South Station and New Bedford or Fall River of approximately 90–100 minutes, varying by train and time of day . 
- Fares and zones: Stations are assigned to MBTA Commuter Rail fare zones. The terminal stations at Fall River and New Bedford are in the highest outer zones, with intermediate stations assigned accordingly; fares follow MBTA’s zone-based pricing and reduced fare programs . 
- Rolling stock and operator: Service is operated by Keolis Commuter Services under contract to the MBTA using standard MBTA diesel push–pull commuter rail equipment (locomotive-hauled bi-level and single-level coaches) . 
- Integration and connections: The South Coast Rail branches integrate into the MBTA Commuter Rail network, sharing trunk routing to South Station. Local bus connections are available via the Southeastern Regional Transit Authority (SRTA) at the downtown Fall River and New Bedford stations and adjacent bus facilities .

## Governance, funding, and cost

- Agencies: MassDOT owns the South Coast Rail corridor segments (Fall River and New Bedford Secondaries) and serves as the program sponsor; the MBTA is responsible for service planning, capital delivery, and operations through its commuter rail operating contract . 
- Environmental review: The Stoughton alignment completed an FEIR/FEIS (2013) and received a federal ROD (2017); the Middleborough Phase 1 received an FRA FONSI (2020) . 
- Funding and delivery: Phase 1 was funded primarily by Commonwealth bond authorizations in the MassDOT/MBTA capital program, with procurement packages covering track, signal, station, bridge, grade crossing, and layover works. MBTA Board and MassDOT program updates have reported a Phase 1 total program budget on the order of approximately $1.3 billion, inclusive of construction, design, property, and contingencies . 
- Contracting: Major construction packages were delivered through conventional design–bid–build and selected design–build elements; program management, environmental, and design services were contracted to industry consultants under MassDOT/MBTA procurements .

## Ridership

- Planning projections: Environmental and planning documents projected several thousand average weekday boardings upon stabilization of service, with demand distributed between the New Bedford and Fall River branches and additional incremental demand expected under the full Stoughton build (Phase 2) . 
- Early results: Following the July 2024 opening, initial news coverage reported strong interest and early ridership activity on launch-day and opening-week trains. The MBTA publishes system performance data; however, disaggregated, validated line-level ridership series specific to South Coast Rail may lag initial launch or be aggregated with the broader Old Colony region in early reports . Where the MBTA has not published official line-level ridership figures, precise counts are not available in agency sources .

## Freight use and coordination

- Ownership and rights: MassDOT’s ownership of the Fall River and New Bedford Secondaries preserves common-carrier freight service; the Commonwealth has contracted Mass Coastal Railroad as the designated freight operator on these South Coast corridors . 
- Coordination: Project works included freight-compatible track improvements, passing capacity, and grade crossing upgrades. The MBTA/Keolis dispatcher coordinates passenger slots with the freight operator, consistent with the operating agreements and safety protocols . 

## Environmental and community impacts

- Environmental considerations were a major focus of the South Coast Rail reviews. The combined FEIR/FEIS for the Stoughton alignment (2013) detailed wetlands impacts, wildlife and habitat issues, noise and vibration, and community considerations, including the crossing of the Hockomock Swamp Area of Critical Environmental Concern. The USACE ROD (2017) documented the federal decision and required mitigation . 
- For Phase 1 via Middleborough, the 2020 FRA FONSI concluded that, with specified mitigation and improvements, the Middleborough approach would not result in significant environmental impacts. Mitigations included wetland restoration/replication, stormwater improvements, noise and vibration mitigation where warranted, grade crossing safety upgrades, and measures to protect cultural and historic resources . 
- Community engagement occurred through MassDOT/MBTA public meetings, design reviews, and station-area planning with municipalities along the route .

## Future plans and status (as of December 12, 2025)

- Phase 2 (Stoughton alignment): The state’s long-term plan remains to construct the Stoughton route to provide a more direct connection between Boston and Taunton/Fall River/New Bedford, consistent with the 2013 FEIR/FEIS and 2017 federal ROD. MassDOT/MBTA materials indicate the project is advancing planning and preliminary engineering for Phase 2 subject to funding availability; as of late 2025, construction of Phase 2 has not been fully funded nor scheduled for delivery, and additional permitting, design updates, and budget development are ongoing . 
- Near-term program: In the interim, MassDOT and the MBTA continue to operate and refine Phase 1 services, monitor ridership and on-time performance, and coordinate with municipalities on station access and transit-oriented development in the Fall River and New Bedford station areas . 

## Notability and significance

- South Coast Rail reconnects Fall River and New Bedford—the largest Massachusetts cities without passenger rail service for decades—to the Boston regional rail network. State and local officials and media coverage described the opening as a major regional mobility improvement expected to reduce travel times for some commuters, broaden access to jobs and education, and support economic development initiatives in the South Coast region . 
- The program has also been notable for its extensive environmental review, the decision to phase implementation with an initial Middleborough service, and the long planning horizon to complete the Stoughton alignment . 

## Stations (Phase 1)

- Middleborough (Middleborough) — opened July 1, 2024 . 
- East Taunton (Taunton) — opened July 1, 2024 . 
- Freetown (Freetown/Assonet) — opened July 1, 2024 . 
- Fall River (Fall River) — opened July 1, 2024 . 
- Church Street (New Bedford) — opened July 1, 2024 . 
- New Bedford (New Bedford) — opened July 1, 2024 .

## See also

- MBTA Commuter Rail . 
- Mass Coastal Railroad .

South Coast Rail
================

Connecting Boston and Southeastern Massachusetts

The South Coast Rail project will restore commuter rail service between Boston and southeastern Massachusetts. Taunton, Fall River and New Bedford are the only major cities within 50 miles of Boston that do not currently have commuter rail access to Boston. South Coast Rail will reconnect this region to jobs and generate economic development.

1.title: South Coast Rail | Projects
1.description: Official website of the MBTA -- schedules, maps, and fare information for Greater Boston's public transportation system, including subway, commuter rail, bus routes, and boat lines.
1.content:
![Image 1: Two trains pulled into the platforms at East Taunton Commuter Rail station](https://cdn.mbta.com/sites/default/files/styles/max_2600x2600/public/media/2025-04/2025-03-24-south-coast-rail-east-taunton-opening.jpg?itok=BPrgcX6B)

The East Taunton station platform on the first day of Fall River/New Bedford Line service (March 24, 2025)

About This Project
------------------

![Image 2: Newly renovated New Bedford station with station sign and platform with yellow tactile surface indicator ](https://cdn.mbta.com/sites/default/files/styles/max_2600x2600/public/media/2024-06/2024-04-SCR-New-Bedford-Renovated-Station-Platform.jpg?itok=F511KnUe)

New Bedford station platform (April 2024)

The [South Coast Rail project](https://www.mass.gov/south-coast-rail) offers a reliable transit connection between southeastern Massachusetts and Boston. Riders can take a one-seat trip for the first time since the late 1950s.

The project creates connections between Boston and the communities of Taunton, New Bedford, and Fall River, the only three major cities within 50 miles of Boston that previously didn’t have Commuter Rail access.

[Learn more about the South Coast Rail Program](https://www.mass.gov/service-details/about-the-south-coast-rail-project)

Building a Better T
-------------------

As part of our $9.6 billion, [5-year capital investment plan](https://www.mbta.com/cip), we're renovating stations, modernizing fare collection systems, upgrading services for our buses, subways, and ferries, and improving the accessibility of the entire system.

[Learn more](https://www.mbta.com/projects)

Schedules
---------

On weekdays, trains run every 70 minutes. There are 32 direct trips to or from [South Station](https://www.mbta.com/stops/place-sstat) including:

*   15 trips between South Station and Fall River
*   17 trips between South Station and New Bedford

On weekends, there are 26 total trips with trains running every two hours.

[View the Fall River/New Bedford Line schedule](https://www.mbta.com/schedules/CR-NewBedford/timetable)

[Check alerts for the Fall River/New Bedford Line](https://www.mbta.com/schedules/CR-NewBedford/alerts)

### Scheduled Transfers at East Taunton Station

In addition to the 32 direct trips to or from South Station on weekdays, we operate connecting trains between:

*   Fall River Depot and East Taunton station
*   New Bedford station and East Taunton station

Riders can transfer between connecting trains and direct trains at East Taunton station where the Fall River and New Bedford branches meet. This means riders on both branches can access more trips to or from South Station throughout the weekday.

For example, riders going between New Bedford and South Station can get to their destination even if the next direct trip is between Fall River and South Station:

1.   At New Bedford station, board the connecting train going to East Taunton station.
2.   At East Taunton station, exit the connecting train to make a transfer.
3.   Board the direct train that came from Fall River Depot and is continuing to South Station.

1.   At South Station, board the direct train going to Fall River Depot.
2.   At East Taunton station, exit the direct train to make a transfer.
3.   Board the connecting train going to New Bedford station.

We've coordinated train schedules to ensure that riders always have enough time to transfer at East Taunton.

* * *

Safety First Program
--------------------

**Safety First** is a program that educates people on how to stay safe around train tracks. Our goal is to bring an understanding of safety rules to all residents in every southeastern Massachusetts city and town.

Through presentations, brochures, videos, meetings, and conversations, you’ll learn safety basics.You can watch and share our [Safety Video Series](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLpgUaADAtNfuJKpPGysCprwkepiOC-DBZ) developed for children, teens, and the general public to learn about the importance of safety for everyone throughout the region.

Watch our safety videos, and please think **Safety First**.

To request rail safety education or materials, call Customer Support at [617-222-3200](tel:617-222-3200) or fill out our[Customer Support form](https://www.mbta.com/customer-support).

[Download a Safety First fact sheet](https://cdn.mbta.com/sites/default/files/2023-12-safety-first-fact-sheet.pdf)(PDF, 926 KB)

[### Commuter Rail Safety](https://www.mbta.com/safety/commuter-rail-safety)
![Image 3: Bi-level Commuter Rail coaches at the newly-completed Freetown Station](https://live-mbta.pantheonsite.io/sites/default/files/styles/teaser/public/media/2023-03/2023-3-3-cr-scr-freetown-ribbon-cutting-double-car-view.jpg?itok=9iFomq_d)

Commuter Rail safety is important to the MBTA. We aim to educate our riders and community members about Commuter Rail safety to prevent any accidents or close calls.

[Learn more](https://www.mbta.com/safety/commuter-rail-safety)

Construction Timeline
---------------------

South Coast Rail is being built in phases:

*   **Phase 1:** Extended the former Middleborough/Lakeville Line, now named the Fall River/New Bedford Line. Service on the [Fall River/New Bedford Line](https://www.mbta.com/schedules/CR-NewBedford/timetable) started March 24, 2025.
*   **Full Build:** Extends the Stoughton Line south to connect more communities to the Fall River/New Bedford Line.

Phase 1 broke ground in July 2019, with major construction beginning in 2020. After we completed construction of stations, tracks, and signals, we also conducted rigorous testing to meet safety certifications and qualifications that precede passenger service.

Construction was divided into two contracts, with early action work preceding both:

*   Construction of the Fall River Secondary Line, which will connect Fall River to Boston
*   Construction of the New Bedford Main Line, the Middleborough Secondary Line, and the signal system for the entire Phase 1 corridor, which will connect Taunton, New Bedford, and Fall River to Boston

[See a map of the Phase 1 corridor](https://cdn.mbta.com/sites/default/files/2024-12-18-south-coast-rail-phase-1-corridor-map-updated.pdf)(PDF, 9.1 MB)

![Image 4: A crew works on culvert installation in Lakeville as part of the South Coast Rail project (May 2020)](https://cdn.mbta.com/sites/default/files/styles/max_650x650/public/media/2020-05/SCR_Culvert_Installation2020.jpg?itok=7KdZdwqv)

A crew replaces rail above a completed culvert installation in Lakeville as part of the South Coast Rail project (May 2020)

Our crews completed early action work in fall 2020 in preparation for Phase 1 construction:

*   Replaced four railroad bridges
*   Installed 46 culverts as part of the drainage system
*   Ordered and stored long-lead special track materials in advance to reduce construction delays
*   Constructed five wetland mitigation areas and began monitoring their success

[Learn more about early action work](https://www.mass.gov/lists/south-coast-rail-documents-and-meeting-materials#spring-2019-fact-sheet-)

![Image 5: 16 bi-level coaches, like the one pictured here, will be put into service as part of the South Coast Rail project ](https://cdn.mbta.com/sites/default/files/styles/max_650x650/public/media/2020-05/SCR_Bi-levelCoach.jpg?itok=-3Jgz3cU)

16 bi-level coaches, like the one pictured here, will be put into service during Phase 1 of the South Coast Rail project

In October 2019, the Fiscal and Management Control Board (FMCB) [approved the purchase of 16 bi-level coaches](https://www.mbta.com/news/2019-09-23/fmcb-approves-the-procurement-80-new-commuter-rail-bi-level-coaches) to meet the needs of the South Coast Rail project. The refurbishment of two locomotives required for South Coast Rail service is also complete. As of summer 2023, these vehicles are part of the state's commuter rail system inventory.

*   ![Image 6: Newly completed Freetown Station platform](https://cdn.mbta.com/sites/default/files/styles/max_650x650/public/media/2023-03/2023-3-3-cr-scr-freetown-ribbon-cutting-platform-view.jpg?itok=rACkugcF)

The Completed Freetown Station during the ribbon-cutting event celebrating the substantial completion of the Fall River Secondary Line contract (December 2022) 
*   The Fall River Secondary Line extends to Fall River through Freetown and Taunton, providing direct service between Fall River and Boston.This new Commuter Rail line includes two stations in Freetown and Fall River, and a layover facility at Weaver’s Cove in Fall River. We completed construction at the end of 2024.

**Completed Work**

Crews reconstructed 12.1 miles of the Fall River Secondary Line, which was previously a freight line, to lift speed restrictions and allow for Commuter Rail service. Work also included tree clearing, erosion control, and survey work along the tracks. The tracks were reconstructed, resulting in improved freight service in the region.

Construction included the following:

*   Nine rail bridges
*   10 new grade crossings and four interlockings
*   Two new stations and a layover facility for storing trains overnight

Trains on the completed Fall River Secondary Line travel through Berkley, Freetown, and Fall River.

[See a map of the Fall River Secondary Line](https://cdn.mbta.com/sites/default/files/2020-05/SCR_FRS_Map.pdf)

![Image 7: view of rail layover yard with blue sky](https://cdn.mbta.com/sites/default/files/styles/max_650x650/public/media/2025-01/2024-09-10-scr-wamsutta-layover-yard.jpeg?itok=BrdJ5T4o)

Wamsutta layover yard (September 2024)

The Middleborough Secondary Line extends from Middleborough through Taunton and into New Bedford to provide direct service between New Bedford and Boston.

The new Commuter Rail line includes four stations and a layover facility adjacent to the existing one in Wamsutta.

We completed construction for the Middleborough Secondary and New Bedford Main lines in fall 2024. We completed construction for the pedestrian bridge at [New Bedford](https://www.mbta.com/stops/place-NBM-0546) station in spring 2025.

**Completed Work**

Crews reconstructed 24.1 miles of Middleborough Secondary and the New Bedford Main lines, which are currently active freight lines, to lift speed restrictions and allow for Commuter Rail service. The right-of-way (ROW) was also reconstructed, resulting in improved freight service in the region.

Construction included:

*   Six rail bridges, constructed to meet state-of-good-repair guidelines
*   18 grade crossings and 14 interlockings
*   Four new stations and a layover facility for storing trains overnight
*   Signal systems and [positive train control (PTC)](https://www.mbta.com/projects/commuter-rail-positive-train-control-ptc) for the entire Phase 1 corridor

Work took place in Middleborough, Taunton, Lakeville, Freetown, and New Bedford. Testing for the entire South Coast Rail occurred under this contract.

Work has been completed on the Fall River Secondary Line to overlay signals and communications.

[See a map of the Middleborough Secondary and New Bedford lines](https://cdn.mbta.com/sites/default/files/2020-05/SCR_MSNBML_map.pdf)

[Read the press release](https://www.mbta.com/news/2020-08-24/fmcb-approves-4035-million-contract-south-coast-rail-main-line-construction)

The Full Build will extend Commuter Rail service on the Stoughton Main Line and Northeast Corridor (north of Canton Junction). It will bring service to Taunton and connect more communities in the region.

This stage presents more challenges related to wetland impacts, complex engineering, electrification, and cost. The next steps include starting conceptual design work, preliminary engineering, and securing funding.

[See a map of the Full Build corridor](https://cdn.mbta.com/sites/default/files/2020-05/SCR_FullBuild_CorridorMap_2020.pdf) (PDF, 793 KB)

How to Pay Your Commuter Rail Fare
----------------------------------

### First, choose how you'll pay your fare

Conductors will check your ticket or pass after you board the train.

During [Fare Is Fair](https://mbta.com/fares/fare-fair) events, your ticket may be checked at any point during your trip, including before you board or after you get off the train.

**Note:** CharlieCards are not accepted on Commuter Rail with the exception of cards with monthly Commuter Rail passes. These cards are printed with the month and zone of the pass and can be used to pay for both bus/subway and Commuter Rail.

CharlieTicket

Best for frequent Commuter Rail riders who also take the subway or bus

Monthly passes available (1-Day and 7-Day passes also available for Zone 1A)

 No online card management

 No discounts

One-way and round trip tickets valid on:

 Commuter Rail, up to designated zone

Monthly passes valid on:

 Commuter Rail, up to designated zone

 Subway

 Bus

 Charlestown Ferry

 East Boston Ferry(seasonal)

 Hingham/Hull Ferry with Zone 6 passes and up

Note: Interzone passes not valid on subway, Express Bus, and ferry

mTicket

Best for infrequent Commuter Rail riders or pass holders who don't often take subway or bus

 $10 discount on monthly passes

 10% discount for 5-day Flex Pass

 Convenient smartphone app for ticket purchase and validation

 Option to purchase multiple tickets

 Only one monthly pass per app or device

 No transfers

Valid on:

Commuter Rail, up to designated zone

 All MBTA ferries

[](https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/mbta-mticket/id560487958?mt=8)[](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.mbta.mobileapp)

Cash Onboard

Best for infrequent Commuter Rail riders at stations where tickets can’t be purchased at fare vending machines or ticket windows

 May include a $3 fee if you board at a station where tickets can be purchased

Only available for one-way and round trip tickets

 Not available during Fare is Fair events

### Then, choose where to buy your ticket or pass

 mTicket app 

One-way, round trip, 5-day Flex Passes, reduced fare and monthly Commuter Rail passes for all zones are available on the mTicket App.

Credit and debit cards are accepted.

**[](https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/mbta-mticket/id560487958?mt=8)[](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.mbta.mobileapp&hl=en)**

[Watch an instructional video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?time_continue=1&v=6gBcPlPsm9k)

For issues with the mTicket app you can email [customerservice@keoliscs.com](mailto: customerservice@keoliscs.com) or call [617-222-3200](tel: 617-222-3200).

 Ticket booths 

You can purchase one-way, round trip, and monthly Commuter Rail passes for all zones and reduced fare 10-ride ticket bundles from agents at:

*   [North Station](https://www.mbta.com/stops/place-north)
*   [South Station](https://www.mbta.com/stops/place-sstat)
*   [Back Bay Station](https://www.mbta.com/stops/place-bbsta)

If you need to upgrade a pass to a higher zone you can visit the booths are North or South Station, or the Charlie Service Center. You will be charged for the price difference. If you are downgrading a pass, refunds will not be issued.

Cash and credit/debit cards are accepted.

 Fare vending machines 

One-way, round trip, and monthly Commuter Rail passes up to Zone 10* are available at fare vending machines, which are located at all subway stations and the [Lynn](https://www.mbta.com/stops/Lynn) and [Worcester/Union](https://www.mbta.com/stops/Worcester) Commuter Rail stations.

Most machines accept cash, major credit/debit cards, and EBT cards. Some machines only accept credit/debit/EBT cards and are marked to indicate that they don’t accept cash.

* Interzone tickets and passes are not available from fare vending machines.

 Online 

You can order monthly Commuter Rail passes for all zones online. Passes will be mailed to you.

Credit and debit cards are accepted.

[Buy a monthly Commuter Rail pass online](https://commerce.mbta.com/Passes/)

You can also sign up for Auto-pay, a monthly Commuter Rail pass that automatically renews each month.

[Sign up for Auto-pay](https://www.mbta.com/fares/auto-pay/auto-pay-commuter-rail?utm_source=Web-CRFares-Tab&utm_medium=web&utm_campaign=CRFares)

 Retail sales locations 

You can purchase one-way, round trip, and monthly Commuter Rail passes up to Zone 10 at retail stores around Greater Boston and Providence.

Cash and credit/debit cards are accepted. Some locations also accept EBT cards.

[Find a retail store near you](https://www.mbta.com/fares/retail_sales_locations)

You can also use your EBT card to load value or passes onto a CharlieTicket at fare vending machines, the [Charlie Service Center](https://www.mbta.com/fares/charliecard-store), and MBTA retail sales locations that accept EBT cards.

[Learn how to pay with your EBT card](https://www.mbta.com/fares/use-your-ebt-card-the-mbta)

Passes
------

The price of your monthly Commuter Rail pass depends on which zones your boarding and exiting stations are located in.

Monthly passes can be purchased at fare vending machines or on mTicket starting on the 15th of the month prior. Printed passes need to be ordered between the 15th and 22nd of the month prior to be shipped.

**Note:**[Reduced monthly Commuter Rail passes](https://www.mbta.com/fares/reduced#crpasses) are available for eligible riders. Passes can be purchased on either a CharlieTicket or via the mTicket app.

Monthly Commuter Rail Pass CharlieTicket

$90.00 – $426.00

Unlimited travel for 1 calendar month

Valid on:

*    Commuter Rail, up to designated pass zone
*    Subway
*    Bus
*    Charlestown Ferry
*    East Boston Ferry (seasonal)
*    Hingham/Hull Ferry with Zone 6 passes and up
*    Lynn Ferry with Zone 2 passes and up(seasonal)

Please note:

*   Zone 1A passes not valid on Express Bus
*   Interzone passes not valid on subway, Express Bus, and ferry

Valid on:

No transfers to other modes

*   Valid Saturdays and Sundays
*   Available onboard trains, at ticket windows, and from mTicket

Valid only on:

 Commuter Rail

5-day Flex Pass

### $21.60 - $119.25

*   Get five 1-day passes for a 10% discount compared to round-trip travel
*   1-day passes valid for 24 hours of unlimited travel
*   Use passes anytime within 30-days after purchase
*   Available only in the mTicket app

Valid only on:

 Commuter Rail, up to designated pass zone

No transfers to other modes

**Note:** All Commuter Rail passes for one-way and round-trip travel expire 90 days from the purchase date.

Commuter Rail Fare Zones
------------------------

Each Commuter Rail station is located in a fare zone, from 1A – 10. Your Commuter Rail fare depends on which zones your boarding and exiting stations are located in.

[Learn more about Commuter Rail zones](https://www.mbta.com/fares/commuter-rail-fares/zones)

[Download a Commuter Rail zones map](https://www.mbta.com/cr-map-zones)

Use Your CharlieCard on the Commuter Rail
-----------------------------------------

You can use your CharlieCard to pay for travel within [Fairmount Line Zone 1A](https://www.mbta.com/projects/fairmount-line-weekday-service-pilot). Tap your CharlieCard at the fare validators on the platform.

[Learn more about CharlieCards](https://www.mbta.com/fares/charliecard)

[![Image 6: A Commuter Rail rider wearing a face covering uses his CharlieCard at a fare validator at Blue Hill Ave Station.](https://cdn.mbta.com/sites/default/files/styles/whats_happening/public/media/2020-06/commuter-rail-blue-hill-fvm%20060120.jpg?itok=Z67OIxPM)](https://www.mbta.com/fares/charliecard "Learn more about CharlieCards")

Get monthly passes—at pre-tax rates—through your employer.

[Learn more about Perq](https://perq.mbta.com/for-employees)

### When you're ready to board the train

The conductor will verify your fare payment after you board the train. The conductor may tuck a small piece of paper on the seat back in front of you to indicate that you paid your fare.

The only exception to this is during [Fare Is Fair](https://www.mbta.com/fares/fare-fair) events, when your ticket may be checked at any point during your trip, including before you board or after you get off the train.

 Pay with a prepaid ticket or pass 

![Image 8: charlieticket-single-ride.jpg](https://cdn.mbta.com/sites/default/files/fares/charlieticket-single-ride.jpg)

Show your ticket or pass to the conductor.

 Pay with mTicket 

![Image 10: mticket-app-ticket-activation.jpg](https://cdn.mbta.com/sites/default/files/fares/mticket-app-ticket-activation.jpg)

1.   Open the mTicket App.
2.   Activate the ticket you would like to use.
3.   Show it to the conductor for verification.

Tickets are valid for **three hours**after activation. Please note, once a ticket is activated, it cannot be deactivated.

 Pay with cash or credit on board 

![Image 12: commuter-rail-rider.JPG](https://cdn.mbta.com/sites/default/files/fares/commuter-rail-rider.JPG)

1.   Tell the conductor you would like to pay in cash or with a credit card. They will ask you where you are going, and if you’d like a one-way or round-trip ticket.
2.   Pay the conductor. Keep in mind this may include a $3 fee if you boarded at a station where you could have purchased a ticket at a fare vending machine or ticket window.
3.   The conductor will give you a paper ticket with your origin and destination listed on it. If you’re going round trip, keep this ticket for your return.

Please note that this option is not available during [Fare Is Fair](https://www.mbta.com/fares/fare-fair) events.

About
=====

### When the First and Last Miles are the Most Important

For over a decade, the Mass Coastal Railroad has provided integrated rail freight and logistics services to businesses and industries throughout the South Coast of Massachusetts and Southern New England.

Our railroad operates a network of lines totaling 135 route miles of track stretching from Fall River to Hyannis, and is custodian of an additional 42 miles of track. The Mass Coastal prides itself on providing personalized, six day per week service for our customers. Utilizing Mass Coastal’s services, customers can quickly and easily reach all of the Cape and the Islands, the greater metro Boston market, central Massachusetts, Rhode Island, and everywhere in between.

In this brochure is a guide to the services available on the Mass Coastal. At facilities throughout our system, shippers can take advantage of a variety of logistics options, including warehousing/cross dock, climate controlled warehousing, steel/lumber reloads, bulk products transloading, public tracks, and FTZ port services. Our facilities are run both by the Mass Coastal and trusted 3PL partners who are experts in their fields.

Commodities handled include:

*   Plastics
*   Chemicals
*   Aggregates
*   General consumer goods
*   Food grade (including chilled and frozen)
*   Steel
*   MSW/C&D
*   Lumber and building products
*   Ferrous and non-ferrous scrap
*   Feed, grains, and soybeans

The Mass Coastal interchanges daily with our Class 1 interchange partner CSX at two locations – Taunton and Middleboro. Through our partnership with CSX, shippers can ship products and materials to and from any location in the United States, Canada, and Mexico.
